Chapter 12. The Work Ahead: Redrawing the Lines
If there’s one thing we can learn from the story of segregation, it’s this—our world isn’t set in stone. Every line that divides us was drawn by people, and you know what? We can redraw those lines, too. The work ahead isn’t only about changing policies. It’s about stretching our imaginations, finding the courage to do what’s right, and being willing to step up and take action.
Picture this: a city council sitting around a table, debating whether to open up a wealthy neighborhood to more affordable housing. Some folks worry. They wonder what this change might bring for their community. But others? They see an opening—a real chance to unlock doors that have stayed closed for far too long.
Or think about a group of parents who decide they won’t settle for less when it comes to their kids’ school. They come together, push for better funding, and make it clear their children deserve every opportunity. Or maybe it’s a young person, learning their city’s history, who gets inspired to run for office—because they believe they can make a difference.
The truth is, this work can feel slow. There are plenty of barriers along the way. But every single step counts. Every new law, every investment in a neighborhood that’s been left behind, every honest conversation about our past—that’s all movement toward a society that’s fairer and more just.
Most people don’t always notice the power of these small changes. They see the headlines, the setbacks, those moments when it looks like progress has stalled. But underneath it all, the lines are shifting. The story isn’t finished yet—it’s still being written, and every action shapes what comes next.
